binding_amendments.title: Distinguish closed future grants from an already issued ACK
binding_amendments.issue: Closing the runner latch or observing a signal cannot retract a complete ACK the wrapper already validated. A native launch may race cancellation after ACK and before Popen; a filesystem latch read has its own race. The current absolute wording that a closed launch latch means no native Popen is ambiguous between runner and local wrapper state.
binding_amendments.required_selection_text: Closing the runner latch forbids new ACKs. An issued ACK remains a bounded one-shot capability for its already-retained wrapper group until expiry/local cancellation; a launch racing runner cancellation remains custody-owned and is drained. Wrapper-observed signal/error irreversibly closes its local launch path and cannot be reopened by a later ACK. Do not claim zero post-runner-cancel native launches without a separately demonstrated revocation mechanism.
binding_amendments.test_focus: Outer cancellation after durable ACK but before child launch must retain group ownership and fail/clean or preserve scratch honestly, whether child starts or not. This requires no additional service or protocol phase.
